modules.title: Data Warehousing and Star Schema
modules.goal: Model analytical data at a clear grain with facts, dimensions and history.

topics.title: OLTP vs OLAP
topics.simple: OLTP transactions chalata hai; OLAP analysis.
topics.pro: OLTP optimizes many small writes and point reads, while OLAP optimizes large scans, aggregation and historical analysis.

example.sql: -- OLTP: enroll one student; OLAP: enrollments by month

topics.title: Fact Tables
topics.simple: Fact table measures aur foreign keys rakhta hai.
topics.pro: A fact table stores quantitative events at a defined grain, with foreign keys to dimensions.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE fact_enrollments (student_key BIGINT, course_key INTEGER, date_key DATE, count INTEGER);

topics.title: Dimension Tables
topics.simple: Dimension table descriptive context deta hai.
topics.pro: Dimensions describe the who, what, where and when of a fact, with stable keys and attributes.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE dim_student (student_key BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, cohort_month DATE);

topics.title: Star Schema
topics.simple: Star schema fact ko dimensions se jodta hai.
topics.pro: A star schema has a central fact table surrounded by denormalized dimensions, minimizing joins for analytics.

example.sql: SELECT d.month, SUM(f.count) FROM fact_enrollments f JOIN dim_date d ON d.date_key = f.date_key GROUP BY d.month;

topics.title: Snowflake Schema
topics.simple: Snowflake schema dimensions ko normalize karta hai.
topics.pro: A snowflake schema splits dimensions into sub-dimensions, reducing duplication at the cost of more joins.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE dim_course (course_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, department_key INTEGER);

topics.title: Grain
topics.simple: Grain batata hai fact ki ek row kya represent karti hai.
topics.pro: The grain defines exactly what one fact row means, such as one enrollment per student per course.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE fact_enrollments (student_key BIGINT, course_key INTEGER, date_key DATE, PRIMARY KEY (student_key, course_key));

topics.title: Slowly Changing Dimensions
topics.simple: SCD history ya latest value rakhta hai.
topics.pro: Slowly changing dimensions preserve attribute history with version rows or current-value flags.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE dim_student (student_key BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, student_id BIGINT, name TEXT, valid_from DATE, valid_to DATE, is_current BOOLEAN);

topics.title: Surrogate Keys
topics.simple: Warehouse surrogate keys stable integers hote hain.
topics.pro: A warehouse dimension uses a generated surrogate key so source natural keys can change without rewriting facts.
points: Natural key stays as an attribute.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE dim_student (student_key BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, student_id BIGINT UNIQUE, name TEXT);

topics.title: ETL vs ELT
topics.simple: ETL transform before load; ELT after load.
topics.pro: ETL transforms data before loading, while ELT loads raw data and transforms it inside the warehouse.

example.sql: -- ELT: load raw, then transform with SQL

topics.title: Aggregates
topics.simple: Pre-aggregated tables reports fast karte hain.
topics.pro: Aggregate tables store rolled-up measures at a coarser grain for dashboards and repeated reports.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE agg_monthly_enrollments AS SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', enrolled_on) AS month, COUNT(*) AS total FROM enrollments GROUP BY 1;

topics.title: Materialized Views
topics.simple: Materialized view warehouse aggregate cache karta hai.
topics.pro: A materialized view stores a query result and is refreshed on a schedule or after loads.

example.sql: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_monthly_enrollments AS SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', enrolled_on) AS month, COUNT(*) AS total FROM enrollments GROUP BY 1;

topics.title: Conformed Dimensions
topics.simple: Shared dimensions consistent definitions dete hain.
topics.pro: Conformed dimensions use the same keys and attributes across fact tables so metrics can be compared.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE dim_date (date_key DATE PRIMARY KEY, month DATE, year INTEGER);

topics.title: Factless Fact Tables
topics.simple: Factless fact table events ya coverage record karta hai.
topics.pro: A factless fact table records that an event occurred or a relationship exists, without a numeric measure.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE fact_attendance (student_key BIGINT, date_key DATE, PRIMARY KEY (student_key, date_key));

topics.title: Late-Arriving Data
topics.simple: Late data ko correct partition me load karo.
topics.pro: Late-arriving facts must land in the correct historical partition and trigger affected aggregate refreshes.

example.sql: INSERT INTO fact_enrollments VALUES (1, 10, DATE '2026-01-15', 1);

topics.title: Data Quality in Warehouse
topics.simple: Warehouse loads ko validate karo.
topics.pro: Warehouse quality checks catch duplicate facts, unknown dimension keys and impossible measures before publishing.

example.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_enrollments f LEFT JOIN dim_student d ON d.student_key = f.student_key WHERE d.student_key IS NULL;

topics.title: Warehouse Performance
topics.simple: Partition, sort aur pre-aggregate large facts.
topics.pro: Warehouse performance comes from columnar storage, partitioning, compression and pre-aggregation, not OLTP indexes alone.

example.sql: SELECT month, SUM(total) FROM agg_monthly_enrollments GROUP BY month;

topics.title: Common Modeling Errors
topics.simple: Mixed grain, missing keys aur duplicated facts common errors hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are mixing grains in one fact table, lacking dimension keys and reloading duplicates without a merge.

example.sql: SELECT student_key, course_key, COUNT(*) FROM fact_enrollments GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

topics.title: BI Semantic Layer
topics.simple: Semantic layer metrics ko define karta hai.
topics.pro: A semantic layer centralizes metric definitions, joins and access rules so dashboards agree.

example.sql: -- metric: active students = distinct student_key with enrollment in period

topics.title: Warehouse Governance
topics.simple: Ownership, lineage aur retention define karo.
topics.pro: Governance assigns owners, tracks lineage and sets retention and access policies for warehouse data.

example.sql: -- document source, owner and refresh for each table

topics.title: Practical Star Schema
topics.simple: Fact aur dimensions ko grain ke saath design karo.
topics.pro: A practical star schema starts from the business question, declares the grain, then adds conformed dimensions and measures.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE fact_enrollments (student_key BIGINT, course_key INTEGER, date_key DATE, count INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY (student_key, course_key, date_key));

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain OLTP vs OLAP in a production query.
interview.answer: OLTP optimizes many small writes and point reads, while OLAP optimizes large scans, aggregation and historical analysis. Key rules: OLTP is normalized. OLAP is denormalized. They have different workloads.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Fact Tables in a production query.
interview.answer: A fact table stores quantitative events at a defined grain, with foreign keys to dimensions. Key rules: Measures are numeric. Foreign keys to dimensions. The grain is explicit.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Dimension Tables in a production query.
interview.answer: Dimensions describe the who, what, where and when of a fact, with stable keys and attributes. Key rules: Descriptive attributes. One row per member. Surrogate keys are common.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Star Schema in a production query.
interview.answer: A star schema has a central fact table surrounded by denormalized dimensions, minimizing joins for analytics. Key rules: One fact table. Flat dimensions. Simple joins.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Snowflake Schema in a production query.
interview.answer: A snowflake schema splits dimensions into sub-dimensions, reducing duplication at the cost of more joins. Key rules: More normalized. More joins. Star is simpler for BI.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Grain in a production query.
interview.answer: The grain defines exactly what one fact row means, such as one enrollment per student per course. Key rules: Declare the grain. Never mix grains. Aggregate after the fact.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Slowly Changing Dimensions in a production query.
interview.answer: Slowly changing dimensions preserve attribute history with version rows or current-value flags. Key rules: Type 1 overwrites. Type 2 adds versions. Type 3 keeps limited history.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Surrogate Keys in a production query.
interview.answer: A warehouse dimension uses a generated surrogate key so source natural keys can change without rewriting facts. Key rules: Generated integer. Stable for facts. Natural key stays as an attribute.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain ETL vs ELT in a production query.
interview.answer: ETL transforms data before loading, while ELT loads raw data and transforms it inside the warehouse. Key rules: ETL uses external compute. ELT uses warehouse compute. Both need orchestration.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Aggregates in a production query.
interview.answer: Aggregate tables store rolled-up measures at a coarser grain for dashboards and repeated reports. Key rules: Define the grain. Refresh on schedule. Document freshness.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Materialized Views in a production query.
interview.answer: A materialized view stores a query result and is refreshed on a schedule or after loads. Key rules: Good for repeated reports. Needs refresh. Can be indexed.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Conformed Dimensions in a production query.
interview.answer: Conformed dimensions use the same keys and attributes across fact tables so metrics can be compared. Key rules: Share keys. Share definitions. Govern changes.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Factless Fact Tables in a production query.
interview.answer: A factless fact table records that an event occurred or a relationship exists, without a numeric measure. Key rules: No measure. Counts are derived. Useful for coverage.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Late-Arriving Data in a production query.
interview.answer: Late-arriving facts must land in the correct historical partition and trigger affected aggregate refreshes. Key rules: Detect late data. Load to the right date. Refresh affected aggregates.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Data Quality in Warehouse in a production query.
interview.answer: Warehouse quality checks catch duplicate facts, unknown dimension keys and impossible measures before publishing. Key rules: Check keys. Check duplicates. Check measures.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Warehouse Performance in a production query.
interview.answer: Warehouse performance comes from columnar storage, partitioning, compression and pre-aggregation, not OLTP indexes alone. Key rules: Partition by date. Pre-aggregate. Scan fewer columns.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Common Modeling Errors in a production query.
interview.answer: Common failures are mixing grains in one fact table, lacking dimension keys and reloading duplicates without a merge. Key rules: One grain per fact. Keys everywhere. Idempotent loads.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain BI Semantic Layer in a production query.
interview.answer: A semantic layer centralizes metric definitions, joins and access rules so dashboards agree. Key rules: Define metrics once. Control joins. Document ownership.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Warehouse Governance in a production query.
interview.answer: Governance assigns owners, tracks lineage and sets retention and access policies for warehouse data. Key rules: Assign owners. Track lineage. Set retention.

interview.q: Module 35 · Explain Practical Star Schema in a production query.
interview.answer: A practical star schema starts from the business question, declares the grain, then adds conformed dimensions and measures. Key rules: Question first. Declare grain. Add dimensions. Add measures.

debug.fix: Split into facts at one grain, or store one row per event and aggregate later.
debug.error: One row mixes revenue and enrollment count at different grains

debug.title: Missing dimension
debug.fix: Insert the dimension row first, then the fact.

debug.title: Duplicate facts
debug.broken: Reload the same fact file twice.
debug.fix: Use a merge or delete-and-insert by load window.

debug.title: SCD overwrite
debug.fix: Close the current version and insert a new one with valid_from.

debug.title: Surrogate key reuse
debug.broken: Reuse student_key 1 for a different student.
debug.fix: Generate a new surrogate key for each dimension version.
debug.error: Facts point to the wrong person

debug.title: No date dimension
debug.fix: Join dim_date and group by its month attribute.
debug.error: Reports cannot use fiscal or holiday attributes

debug.title: Aggregate stale
debug.fix: Refresh the aggregate after the load.

debug.title: Wrong join key
debug.broken: JOIN dim_student d ON d.student_key = f.course_key;
debug.fix: JOIN dim_student d ON d.student_key = f.student_key;
debug.error: The join uses the wrong dimension key

debug.title: Orphan facts
debug.fix: Load dimensions first or use a late-arriving dimension row.

debug.title: No retention
debug.fix: Define retention and archive cold partitions.
